The core is a Rust crate, so a Rust program calls it directly: no binding layer, no generated code.
`ov-core` is the same facade the other languages wrap (`OvClient`, `Account`, `Vault`,
`ServiceAccount`, `SelfHosted`, the records and `OvError`), running on the same code as the iOS,
desktop and web apps and the `ov` CLI.

- Rust 1.98 or later, on any target the core builds for (macOS, Linux, Windows; iOS and Android
  through the other bindings).
- Calls that touch the network or run the account KDF are `async` and take a `CancelToken`. The core
  doesn't depend on an async runtime: tokio, async-std or a plain executor all work.
- You write the Host (HTTP, secure store, offline cache, clock, log sink) or copy one. There's no
  ready-made Host crate.

The API reference is at [developer.openvireo.com/reference/rust](https://developer.openvireo.com/reference/rust/).

## Install

The crates aren't on crates.io. Depend on a release tag of this repository:

```toml
[dependencies]
ov-core = { git = "https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }
```

Cargo finds the crate inside the workspace and resolves its dependencies from the workspace's pinned
versions. `Cargo.lock` then records the commit, so every build uses the same code. Add `ov-share` the
same way if you need `parse_share_link` or the share-link primitives; the other domain crates
(`ov-crypto`, `ov-kdbx`, `ov-merge`, ...) are there too, but only `ov-core` keeps a stable API between
minor releases.

Check the install:

```rust
println!("{}", ov_core::version());   // X.Y.Z
```

The account KDF is Argon2id at 64 MiB. Unoptimised, a sign-in takes seconds, so optimise those crates
in debug builds:

```toml
[profile.dev.package.argon2]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.blake2]
opt-level = 3
```

## A client

An `OvClient` needs a `ClientConfig` (this device) and a `Host`:

```rust
use ov_core::api::{CancelToken, ClientConfig, DeviceInfo, OvClient, Platform};

let client = OvClient::new(
    ClientConfig {
        device: DeviceInfo { id: None, name: "My script".into(), platform: Platform::Cli },
        offline: false,   // true keeps the offline cache: unlock and open vaults without the network
        server: None,
    },
    host,   // see "The Host" below
);
let cancel = CancelToken::new();
let account = client.connect("https://accounts.openvireo.com".into(), cancel.clone()).await?;
```

`connect` fetches the server's discovery document and restores a session the Host's store kept from an
earlier run. Handles (`OvClient`, `Account`, `Vault`, ...) hold an `Arc` inside: clone them freely and
share them between tasks and threads.

## Sign in

```rust
use ov_core::api::{LoginInput, LoginStep};

let mut step = account
    .login(
        LoginInput {
            email: "you@example.com".into(),
            password: password.into_bytes(),
            secret_key: Some(secret_key.into_bytes()),   // None once this device is trusted
            totp: None,
            trust_device: true,
        },
        cancel.clone(),
    )
    .await?;
while let LoginStep::NeedsTotp(challenge) = step {   // two-step sign-in is on
    step = account.submit_totp(challenge, ask_for_code(), cancel.clone()).await?;
}
```

`account.register(RegisterInput { .. })` creates an account and returns the new Secret Key once.
`account.lock()` wipes the keys and keeps the session; `account.unlock(password, None, cancel)` opens
it again. `account.sign_out(false, cancel)` ends the session.

## Vaults and entries

```rust
for info in account.vaults(cancel.clone()).await? {
    println!("{} {:?}", info.name, info.role);   // VaultRole::Read, Write or Manage
}
let vault = account.open_vault(vault_id, cancel.clone()).await?;
for e in vault.entries(false) {
    println!("{}", e.title);
}
let password = vault.read_field("ov://Personal/GitHub/password".into())?;   // Vec<u8>
```

`vault.write_field(reference, value, create, cancel)` edits one field and syncs.

### Add an entry and sync

```rust
use ov_core::api::{EntryInput, FieldInput, SyncOptions};

let field = |name: &str, value: &str| FieldInput { name: name.into(), value: value.as_bytes().to_vec(), protected: None };
vault.add_entry(
    vault.root_group_id(),
    EntryInput {
        fields: vec![field("Title", "Example"), field("UserName", "app"), field("Password", "s3cret")],
        ..Default::default()
    },
)?;
let report = vault.sync(SyncOptions { local_changed: true, accept_server_state: false }, cancel.clone()).await?;
println!("{:?} {:?}", report.outcome, report.conflicts);
```

Edits change the in-memory database. `sync` merges them with the server's copy and uploads.

## Share links

```rust
use ov_core::api::{default_share_fields, item_share_payload, ShareOptions};

let entry = vault.entry(entry_id.clone())?;
let payload = item_share_payload(entry, default_share_fields(), None);
let options = ShareOptions {
    expires_in: 7 * 86400,
    max_opens: Some(1),
    passcode: None,
    vault_id: Some(vault.id()),
    entry_id: Some(entry_id),
};
let link = account.create_share(payload, options, cancel.clone()).await?;
println!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&link.url));   // https://share.openvireo.com/<id>#<key>
```

`client.share_info` and `client.open_share` open a link without an account.

## Errors

Every fallible call returns `Result<T, OvError>`. `OvError` implements `std::error::Error`, so `?`
works with `Box<dyn Error>`, `anyhow` and the rest. Match on `code` (`OvErrorCode`), the same codes
every binding uses:

```rust
use ov_core::OvErrorCode;

match vault.write_field(reference, value, false, cancel.clone()).await {
    Ok(_) => {}
    Err(e) if e.code == OvErrorCode::NetworkError => println!("saved locally; it uploads later"),
    Err(e) if e.code == OvErrorCode::InvalidReference => println!("no such entry or field"),
    Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
}
```

`e.wire_code()` is the code as the server and the other bindings spell it (`"network_error"`),
`e.status` the HTTP status and `e.details` the server's JSON details, when there are any.

## Async and cancellation

The futures are `Send`, so they run on a multi-threaded runtime and inside `tokio::spawn`. Pass a
`CancelToken` to each call and call `cancel()` on it (or a clone of it) from anywhere: the call stops at
its next step and returns `OvErrorCode::Aborted`. A token stays cancelled, so use a fresh one for the
next call.

```rust
let cancel = CancelToken::new();
let task = tokio::spawn({
    let (account, cancel) = (account.clone(), cancel.clone());
    async move { account.vaults(cancel).await }
});
cancel.cancel();
assert!(matches!(task.await?, Err(e) if e.code == OvErrorCode::Aborted));
```

Dropping the future also stops the call.

## Live events

```rust
use ov_core::api::AccountEvent;

let stream = account.subscribe(cancel.clone()).await?;
while let Some(event) = stream.next(cancel.clone()).await? {
    match event {
        AccountEvent::VaultChanged { vault_id, etag, .. } => { /* another device uploaded it */ }
        AccountEvent::VaultsChanged { vaults } => { /* access changed */ }
        AccountEvent::SessionEnded { reason, .. } => break,
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

`stream.close()` from another task makes a pending `next()` return `None`.

## The Host

The core does no I/O. A `Host` holds five trait objects, all in `ov_core::host`:

| Part | Trait | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `http` | `HttpTransport` | Sends requests and opens the events stream |
| `store` | `SecureStore` | Keeps secrets: the session, trusted Secret Keys, self-hosted pairings |
| `cache` | `BlobCache` | The offline cache: vault ciphertext and sync state, all already encrypted |
| `clock` | `Clock` | Milliseconds since the Unix epoch |
| `log` | `LogSink` | The core's log lines (never secrets) |

The async traits use `async_trait`. Two rules for every transport: don't follow redirects, and don't
send or store cookies. The [Rust examples' `host.rs`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-examples-rust/blob/main/src/host.rs)
is a complete one in about 200 lines (reqwest with rustls, memory for the store and the cache) to copy.
The `ov` CLI's Host in [`bins/ov`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/develop/bins/ov/src/host.rs) keeps the store and the cache in files.

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use ov_core::host::Host;

let host = Host {
    http: Arc::new(MyHttp::new()),
    store: Arc::new(MyKeychainStore),   // the OS keychain, so the device stays trusted
    cache: Arc::new(MyFileCache::new(dir)),
    clock: Arc::new(SystemClock),
    log: Arc::new(MyLog),
};
```

With a store and cache that persist, `client.connect` finds the session again on the next run and
`ClientConfig { offline: true, .. }` opens vaults without the network.

## Secrets

Passwords, Secret Keys, field values and tokens go in and come out as `Vec<u8>` (`SecretBytes`, UTF-8
for text). The core wipes the inputs it's given and its own copies. Wipe the outputs you keep, for
example with `zeroize::Zeroizing`.

## Self-hosted servers

```rust
use ov_core::api::{KdbxCredentials, SelfHosted};

let server = match SelfHosted::restore(client.clone(), url.clone()).await? {
    Some(server) => server,   // paired on an earlier run (needs a persistent store)
    None => SelfHosted::pair(client.clone(), url, code, "Laptop".into(), cancel.clone()).await?,
};
let creds = KdbxCredentials { password: Some(password), ..Default::default() };
let result = server.sync_database("personal".into(), std::fs::read(&path)?, creds, cancel.clone()).await?;
std::fs::write(&path, &result.kdbx)?;   // the merged file
```

## Local `.kdbx` files

No account is needed:

```rust
let creds = KdbxCredentials { password: Some(b"pw".to_vec()), ..Default::default() };
let vault = client.open_local(std::fs::read("db.kdbx")?, creds, cancel.clone()).await?;
// ...
std::fs::write("db.kdbx", vault.save_local(cancel.clone()).await?)?;
```

`client.create_local(name, creds, cancel)` makes a new database. `account.import_kdbx(data, creds, mode,
cancel)` turns one into a vault.
